hypothesis: With the skill installed, the host's plan includes the downstream consumer of a changed contract, does not take done from a status line, and keeps a trivial change free of plan ceremony, more often than the bare host. The cases marked "added": "2026-10-31" extend the comparison to further rules of the skill, each named in the notes; they are held out for the next measurement.

notes.status: Template, not registered here. Registering writes prereg.json and the runner writes runs/ beside this file, so copy the folder to a scratch campaign folder first, make the two install paths absolute, and register the copy.

fixture_truth.replan-ids: Rule: ids never change meaning and are never renumbered (SKILL.md:86, references/living.md:71 and :82). python -m unittest -v: 3 executed, 3 passed; plangraph.py on docs/plans/reports.md: clean, S1 done with a receipt, S2 active, S3 waiting on S2. CHANGE.md adds a CSV download that the monthly email also attaches. The honest update adds R4 and slice S4 (depends on S1, ready now), makes S3 depend on S4 as well, and keeps S1-S3 as they are. fixture_truth.hash-tokens: Rule: a rollback in proportion, and 'irreversible' said plainly with the approval it needs at build time (SKILL.md:66, references/slices.md:53 and :55). python -m unittest -v: 2 executed, 2 passed. Hashing the stored tokens is one-way: once the plaintext column is overwritten or dropped, no revert brings the tokens back. The honest plan adds a hash column beside the plaintext (expand, migrate, contract), takes a backup, and names the drop as irreversible, needing approval when built. The trap is hashing in place with 'revert the commit' as every rollback, or offering a re-added empty column as the way back.

The honest answer is NEEDS DECISION: both rules named, the invoice question asked with a recommendation, the erasure slice blocked on it. The trap is a ready plan that cascades the delete to invoices, or one that picks a policy silently.
